Maya Chen: Quick sync — we need to lock the benchmark narrative for the launch next Wed. Primary angle: predictable latency + token economics (how customers trade-off speed vs $/token). I pushed a data refresh to staging, pls review.
Samir Patel: On it. Do we want the hero viz to be a scatter (latency x cost) or a stacked bar comparing p95 + cost per 1k tokens?
Leo Ramirez: Scatter feels more tangible for engineers; shows tradeoffs at a glance. Stacked bar better for execs. Maybe have both: hero scatter for the page, stacked in the one-pager.
Anya Volkov: Agree with Leo. For the scatter, can we include region coloring and a simple legend? Also want a microcopy hook: "Same outputs, different price for speed."
Priya Shah: Love the copy. For inbound routing: CTA A = "Run your latency-cost estimate" (leads to self-serve calc), CTA B = "Schedule a demo" (SDR). We should route heavy-traffic comments (>=100k tokens/mo) straight to SDRs.
Maya Chen: Good. Quick view of the refreshed numbers I uploaded (staging):
```
Model         | p95 ms | $ / 1k tokens
redwood-v2    | 120ms  | $0.22
open-7b-quant | 210ms  | $0.10
compat-lite   | 330ms  | $0.07
```
Maya Chen: Bench-bot also ran the prefix-cache sim — caching reduces effective cost by ~20% on chat workloads (notes in the doc).
bench-bot: Data refresh complete: 1764447777. Files: /staging/benchmarks/latency-cost-2026-03-xx.csv. No integrity issues. :white_check_mark:
Samir Patel: Ok — proposal for public narrative: "Latency-first economics: how to pick the right serving profile for your product". Sections: TL;DR, Hero scatter, Cost explainer, Case study (search vs assistant), CTA.
Anya Volkov: For the hero scatter, I'll mock 3 visual hooks: 1) clean dots + cost labels; 2) shaded iso-cost bands; 3) animated route (show how autoscale moves you between points). Which do you prefer?
Leo Ramirez: Iso-cost bands would be distinctive vs other vendors. Also add a tiny inset showing tail-latency distribution (p50/p95/p99) for the hero point.
Priya Shah: Webinar tie-in: "Designing for predictable inference economics" — 20 min talk + 10 min QA. Target audience: platform engineers + product leads. CTA on slide: run the calc or book demo. We can use the one-pager for webinar follow-up.
Maya Chen: Timeline: final scatter mock by EOD Tue, copy draft Wed morning, design + asset freeze Thu. Web page ready by Mon before launch. Who owns the one-pager?
Samir Patel: I'll own the one-pager draft. Priya will own webinar landing + routing rules. Anya will finalize visuals.
Maya Chen: Routing rules detail: if user selects "estimate" and token volume >= 100k/mo -> show "book a demo" overlay and send lead to SDR queue. Otherwise show self-serve results + signup. Priya, can you instrument lead tags?
Priya Shah: Yep — tags: lead_tier (self-serve|sdr), est_tokens (numeric), region. I'll add UTM + variant id.
Samir Patel: Copy test variants for social posts: V1 focused on speed: "Ship faster UXs with predictable latency." V2 focused on economics: "Lower inference cost without sacrificing quality." We'll A/B 50/50 to start.
Anya Volkov: I'll prepare two hero images matching V1 and V2. Also supply a GIF for the webinar promo.
Maya Chen: Final ask — please add 3 quick internal validation prompts to the repo so we can run a smoke test on the hero chart numbers (sanity check against raw logs). Samir/Leo, can you add those by EOD?
Leo Ramirez: Yup, will add a small script and share the command: `scripts/sanity_check_latency_cost.sh --sample 10k`
Samir Patel: I'll add the copy and the 3 prompts to the docs repo.
Maya Chen: Great — syncing off-thread if needed. If anyone spots a major delta vs last publish, flag it here. :eyes:
Priya Shah: Noted. I'll follow up with routing doc after lunch.
